response.sql: WITH g AS (SELECT orderslink, AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS avg_net, AVG(rebtotal) AS avg_reb FROM fees GROUP BY orderslink), o AS (SELECT AVG(feerate - rebrate) AS overall FROM fees) SELECT AVG(g.avg_reb) AS mean_avg_rebtotal, AVG(g.avg_net) AS mean_avg_net_fee_rate, AVG(g.avg_net - o.overall) AS mean_excess_over_overall FROM g CROSS JOIN o WHERE g.avg_net > o.overall

assumptions.assumption: The overall average net fee rate is the average of (feerate - rebrate) across all individual fee rows, skipping rows where either value is NULL, so orders with more fee rows weigh more.
Fee rows with NULL orderslink form a single group, which SQLite's GROUP BY does by default.
A fee row with a NULL feerate or rebrate has no net rate and is skipped in the net-rate averages. Its rebtotal still counts in the average rebtotal for that order.

alternatives.interpretation: The overall average net fee rate is the mean of the per-order (per-group) average net fee rates, so each order counts equally rather than each fee row.
